title: Wayland: Trackpad gestures are passed in embedded game window, but not standalone
body:
### Tested versions

Tested on dff2b9bb66a01d8c1a207531b0752405c7399124

### System information

Godot v4.7.beta (dff2b9bb6) - Manjaro Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Apr 30 18:50:02 UTC 2026 on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - integrated AMD Radeon Graphics (RADV RENOIR) - AMD Ryzen 9 5900HX with Radeon Graphics (16 threads) - 62.20 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When testing a game using the embedded window (either floating or not), `InputEventPanGesture` and `InputEventMagnifyGesture` events are correctly passed to the game, making it behave similarly to on macOS. When launching it standalone, or from the editor but not embedded, the touchpad acts in a very undesirable mouse emulation mode.

I expect that this is some partial implementation thing that wasn't finished, but if it's not clearly documented it's an unwelcome surprise to have inputs function in such a degraded manner outside of the editor.
While searching for any existing issues I came across #119073 which adds `[b]Note:[/b] [InputEventPanGesture] is only supported on macOS, Android, and Linux (Wayland only). On other platforms, it is never emitted from touch events.` which to me confirms that Linux Wayland is expected to emit gesture events on `master` at this time, though perhaps it's only intended to confirm that for the same event on touchscreens - however on Wayland that only seems to generate `InputEventScreenTouch` and `InputEventScreenDrag` events when I attempt gestures.

### Steps to reproduce

1) Make a scene with a script including input event reporting:
```gdscript
extends Node3D  # or Node2D or whatever

func _input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
	print(event)
```
2) Launch the game in the embedded mode, perform 2finger pinch and pan/scroll gestures on the trackpad over the embedded game window. Note the Output.
3) Untick "Embed Game on Next Play" and press "Run Project" again, and perform the same gestures over the game window. Note the Output.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

It's 2LOC
